findings.description: DashboardConductor.attachCommand's docstring says the field is 'as `attachArgs` spells it', but it's actually populated by `attachCommand({ conductorOf: pid })` in dashboard.service.ts — a different function with a different return type.
findings.body:
This docstring misattributes the field's construction: it says "What the operator types to attach, as `attachArgs` spells it", but `src/core/dashboard.service.ts:78` populates this field with `attachCommand({ conductorOf: pid })`, not `attachArgs`. In `src/claude/session-runtime.service.ts`, `attachArgs(target): string[]` (<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/9b9116ae1543d5b37ca7439eaf75f7bcf5226659/src/claude/session-runtime.service.ts#L538-L541>) returns a raw, unquoted argv array with no shell quoting at all, while `attachCommand(target): string` (<https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/9b9116ae1543d5b37ca7439eaf75f7bcf5226659/src/claude/session-runtime.service.ts#L549-L551>) is the function that joins the tokens and applies `shellWord` quoting — the exact behavior this same docstring's next clause describes ("a pinned target quoted for the shell it is pasted into"). Naming `attachArgs` here would send a reader chasing the wrong seam, one whose return type doesn't even match this field's `string` type.

See: <https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/9b9116ae1543d5b37ca7439eaf75f7bcf5226659/src/core/types/dashboard.types.ts#L27-L34>
findings.suggestion:
/**
   * What the operator types to attach, as `attachCommand` spells it: the `-L`
   * socket, because the window is on the conductor's own tmux server and a
   * bare `attach -t` finds nothing (decision 47), and a pinned target quoted
   * for the shell it is pasted into. Who may be shown it is the reader's
   * call, not the model's.
   */
  attachCommand: string;

findings.description: This Header test fixture still hardcodes the pre-PR unpinned/unquoted attachCommand string ('tmux -L pup-conductor-ab12cd34ef56 attach -t pup-conductor-ab12cd34ef56'), which no longer matches what buildDashboardSnapshot actually produces after this PR (now pinned and single-quoted). The test still passes because its assertion only checks a prefix, but the fixture is now unrepresentative of real runtime output.

The file's top-of-file comment guarantees 'this suite never spawns a real tmux pane', but the new `describe('attachArgs against the installed tmux', ...)` block added by this PR routes around the child_process mock via `vi.importActual` and spawns a real tmux binary, contradicting that guarantee for a future reader who trusts it.

shellWord's JSDoc ('A word a shell takes literally, single-quoted when it would not.') restates the function's own ternary rather than stating a WHY; the actual non-obvious invariant (pinned targets start with '=', which zsh equals-expands) is explained two lines below in attachCommand's docstring instead.

Decision 46 says pinned() 'remains for the two commands that address a session by name and nothing else: the stale-name kill before new-session, and killSession' — this PR adds a third caller (attachArgs), leaving that 'and nothing else' text stale. The codebase's own convention for this situation is an italicized addendum under the original decision (used for decisions 7, 35, 43) or an '(addendum to decision N)' code comment; neither was added here.

This call-site comment ('The line carries the -L socket and pins its target, both the runtime's to spell... and it is quoted...') restates facts already fully documented on attachArgs/attachCommand's own JSDoc in session-runtime.service.ts, with no site-specific payload.

This test comment ('The socket, the pin and the quoting are all the runtime's...') restates the same socket/pin/quoting facts already documented at the attachArgs/attachCommand seam in session-runtime.service.ts.
This test comment near-verbatim restates attachArgs's own JSDoc about the prefix-match hazard and the pin, without assertion-specific payload beyond what the seam already documents.
